review_notes: Reviewed all 41 lines, the power-map and semidirect-map range/injectivity lemmas, the semidirect-product topology definitions, the analogous generic factor-extension result, and the direct consumer. The suggested generalization follows the existing embedding and range-preimage proof pattern; its exact Lean elaboration has not been tested.

findings.problem: The statement is restricted to the power endomorphism of an integral lattice, although the proof’s topological argument only needs a closed embedding of the acting group. This limits reuse for other closed subgroup inclusions into an acting group.
findings.proposed_change: Add a general theorem for groups D and E and a homomorphism f : D →* E with hf : Topology.IsClosedEmbedding f, asserting that SemidirectProduct.map (MonoidHom.id L) f (by intros; rfl) : (L ⋊[ρ.comp f] D) →* (L ⋊[ρ] E) is a closed embedding. Prove its embedding property by the product-homeomorphism argument used here, and prove its range is closed by expressing the range as f.range.comap SemidirectProduct.rightHom and taking the preimage of hf.isClosed_range. Keep the current power-map theorem as the instance f := latticePowerHom n m, using latticePowerHom_isEmbedding and its discrete closed range to supply hf.
findings.benefit: Users can obtain closed embeddings for semidirect products induced by any closed embedding of acting groups, without reproving the same topological argument or requiring an integral-lattice power map. The proposed proof reuses the product-topology and range-preimage methods already present in the reviewed sources.
